mechanism: Compression-to-expansion at the daily horizon with a named short-gamma counterparty. While realised vol sits in the bottom tercile of its 30-day history, the market is in the pinned regime that Glassnode's flow-based GEX work attributes to option dealers being net LONG gamma around the strike cluster (they sell rallies and buy dips, so moves fade and RV prints below IV). A single closed 1h bar whose move is >= 4x the pre-shock 72-bar hourly vol AND that closes outside the 72-bar (3-day) range takes spot out of that cluster; beyond it dealer net gamma flips negative (Glassnode: dealers 'must buy as prices rise and sell as prices fall ... pro-cyclical trading adds fuel to the fire'), and perp market makers who absorbed the shock bar are left with inventory against the move that they unwind by hitting in the shock direction. Both flows are price-insensitive and continue for hours-to-days rather than minutes, which is the horizon the 5-min poller can actually execute (entry at the next 1h open, hold up to 48 bars = 2 days). The thesis is continuation of the shock direction to a 200 bps target before a 200 bps stop.
counterparty: (1) Deribit BTC/ETH option dealers whose long-gamma inventory pinned the range: once spot exits the strike cluster their book is net short gamma and they are forced to re-hedge pro-cyclically (buy after up moves, sell after down moves) regardless of price; alts follow via beta/arb to the BTC/ETH hedging flow. (2) Perp market makers who provided liquidity into the shock bar and now carry inventory against the move; they are forced to unwind in the shock direction to cut inventory risk when realised vol jumps. Both pay because they are risk-limited and vol-limited, not because they have a view.

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np


def signals(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series:
    """Shock-out-of-compression drift (closed 1h bars only).

    Compression: the 72-bar realised vol measured on the bar BEFORE the shock bar is at
    or below the 33rd percentile of its trailing 720-bar history. Shock: the closed bar's
    absolute log return is >= 4x that pre-shock 72-bar vol AND the bar's close also
    breaks the pre-shock 72-bar high/low (so the move leaves the pinned range). Fire in
    the direction of the shock. Re-arm only after 48 bars have passed since the last
    fire. Only current-and-prior bars are used.
    """
    c = df["close"].astype(float)
    h = df["high"].astype(float)
    l = df["low"].astype(float)
    r = np.log(c).diff()
    rv72 = r.rolling(72, min_periods=72).std()
    rv_q = rv72.rolling(720, min_periods=360).quantile(0.33)
    rv_prev = rv72.shift(1)
    compressed = (rv_prev <= rv_q.shift(1))
    hi_prev = h.rolling(72, min_periods=72).max().shift(1)
    lo_prev = l.rolling(72, min_periods=72).min().shift(1)
    shock_up = compressed & (r >= 4.0 * rv_prev) & (c > hi_prev)
    shock_dn = compressed & (r <= -4.0 * rv_prev) & (c < lo_prev)
    raw = np.where(shock_up.fillna(False), 1, np.where(shock_dn.fillna(False), -1, 0))
    out = np.zeros(len(df), dtype=np.int64)
    last = -10**9
    for i in range(len(df)):
        if raw[i] != 0 and i - last >= 48:
            out[i] = raw[i]
            last = i
    return pd.Series(out, index=df.index)
